newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi share index closes 2.15 percent lower.
newsitem.headline: Delhi share index closes 2.15 percent lower.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed sharply lower in line with other bourses, where weaker than expected company results weighed on stocks, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 15.04 points, or 2.15 percent, lower at 685.53.

"The persistent drop in share values on the country's other stock exchanges coupled with a plunge in Indian securities overseas led to the fall in share prices," said a stock broker who asked not to be identified.

Joseph John of brokerage firm Gautam Rohtagi said: "It seems that several measures announced by the finance minister and Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) failed to have any long term positive effect."
On Monday, SEBI announced restrictions on short selling.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark index fell 2.45 percent on Wednesday as weaker than expected company results weighed on values.
Reliance Industries closed 8.65 rupees, or 4.5 percent, lower at 181.70 rupees on heavy selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs), brokers said.
TISCO fell 9.10 rupees, or 5.4 percent, to 159.25 rupees on foreign selling, they said.
State Bank of India dropped 8.65 rupees to 217.95, while Oriental Bank of Commerce shed 3.60 rupees to 71.50 on sustained selling by speculators and investors.
